inputs.drivers: USMCA review; rules of origin; tariffs and China+1; continuity mandates; Mexico-U.S. trade; India PLI; electronics, auto, pharma, and AI hardware; labour, infrastructure, rates, FX, and capex cycles.
inputs.invalidation: Capex slows, trade rules disrupt, infrastructure and security delay ramps, incentives disappoint, valuations are full, or Asia remains more competitive.
inputs.seed_claim: Mexico, North America, India, and selected Southeast Asia may convert tariffs, resilience rules, and incentives into measurable factory, industrial-real-estate, logistics, EMS, and automation demand.
inputs.supporting_evidence: The seed requires projects to become occupancy, rent spreads, rail volume, EMS utilisation, and automation orders within 6-12 months.
inputs.value_chain: Mexican industrial real estate and utilities; cross-border rail and intermodal; EMS in Mexico, India, and Southeast Asia; automation, connectors, sensors, and local components; shipping and China-centric hedges.

objective: Research one nearshoring and regional manufacturing-capacity investment idea.
